I can’t thank BluePearl Animal Hospital enough for the compassion and care they showed during one of the hardest moments of my life. My puppy, Jade, who was also my emotional support animal, became extremely sick, and unfortunately I had to make the heartbreaking decision to put her down. She was only 7 months old—full of love, sweetness, and still trying her best to wag her tail.

The staff gave me all the time I needed to grieve. They allowed me to cry, sit with Jade, and be with her the entire time. She was treated with so much love, attention, and dignity, which meant everything to me.

Today, I picked up her ashes, and the experience brought me so much closure. It was handled more beautifully than I expected. The staff also showed me incredible grace by helping me financially, offering flexible payment arrangements, and being truly understanding during such a difficult time.

I’m grateful I remembered this hospital from years ago—my family cat passed when I was about 10, and now at 23, BluePearl once again cared for my family when we needed it most. If you have a sick family pet and want them treated with compassion and respect, I highly recommend bringing them here.

Thank you, BluePearl, for taking such gentle care of Jade and of me.

text.text: First off, if they offered 10 stars for a review I would be giving VEG all 10! Last week, our pup had a very bad GI issue that came out of no where. A little panic set in and we had to get her to a vet to see what was going on asap. We called ahead of time and they sent over a mobile check in to quicken the process when we arrive. When we got there, the staff was awesome. They were so welcoming, respectful and efficient. They offered snacks and drinks while we waited for an assistant. After a very short wait, they wasted no time. There was a plan to get to the bottom of the issue. The doctor was so nice and polite. They brought out a nicely laid out cost estimate and explain each thing so you understand what is going to happen. There was no pushing and shoving to get you to buy things that are not needed. Without writing a book about our visit. Our pup ended up in thier care for 33 hours total. She was very dehydrated and needed constant fluids until we could get her stomach to settle down. Throughout the very short yet felt like forever couple of days, not once did we think she was in "bad" care. There was updates both morning and night. They encouraged us to call anytime to see how she was doing. They explained each different approach to tackle the issue and also went over the cost each time before doing anything. I would love to include names in this review but we worked with a couple different doctors and staff members thoughout the whole process and they were all professional, respectful, polite and just awesome! They sort of have a "open door policy". They let you back where they are doing the exam, you can watch the ultrasound up close, sit with your pup all day if you would like and stop by 24/7 to say see them. We took her for a walk and they even offered setting up a place to stay the night if we wanted. We have nothing but great things to say about this establishment. In a world full of craziness and not always trustworthy business practices. This place was a breath of fresh air. In a time of stress both for the health of our pup and the high cost to follow. They treat you like a human and not just "another customer". If you ever need to go to an urgent care for your furry friend, I would recommend this place time and time again.

Wish I could give VEG South Tampa one million stars!  We brought our 7yr lab mix Ellie in for vomiting/diarrhea that was going on for 48hrs and we were seen right away. We were assigned a private room to wait with our baby, and the team got to work quickly.  Our Ellie went under sedation to have her bloodwork, ultrasound, and X-rays done and the team included us in EVERY step, letting us love and pet our baby to sleep, and then allowing us to actually come and observe them as they did the X-rays and the ultrasound! It was a great feeling to see what goes on “behind closed doors”. TOTAL TRANSPARENCY FROM START TO FINISH.

The Drs spent a great deal of time explaining what we saw in the images from the X-rays and walked us through everything on the ultrasound. Nurse Lani spent a lot of time educating us on the meds she was giving Ellie and most importantly the WHY.  They even provided us with a call button in our room should we need assistance during wait time (1hr of waiting the whole visit btw), and bonus: also gave us snacks and soda since we all rushed in having no dinner.

Thankfully our Ellie’s bloodwork, X-rays, and ultrasound came back clear and we were sent home with some anti-nausea meds and probiotics, and she’s already on the mend.  ❤️‍🩹 We will NEVER go anywhere else for our ER vet needs.  We cannot thank Dr Davison, Dr Osorio, and Nurse Lani enough.  They took such amazing care of our baby and also of us. If you have an emergency for your babies, THIS IS THE PLACE!!

Dr. Debra Deem Morris, DVM, DACVIM, at Affordable Pet Hospital in Tampa, Florida, consistently withheld important information about my dog, Cohen (an 8-year-old, 8 lb Pomeranian-Poodle), and provided inaccurate details. Dr. Morris informed me that Cohen had a tumor affecting part of his liver, which was detected during an ultrasound she recommended. Following this procedure, a needle biopsy of the tumor was performed, but Dr. Morris was unable to determine whether the tumor was benign or malignant. She claimed to have consulted with an oncologist to assess the biopsy results.

Dr. Morris knew that I would only proceed with surgery if the tumor was benign, as I made it clear to her over the phone. After our conversation, Dr. Morris called me back shortly after (a red flag, but I was just focused on Cohen’s well-being), claiming that the oncologist had confirmed the tumor was benign and advised that we move forward with scheduling the surgery.

On the day of surgery (September 9, 2024), Dr. Morris failed to inform me of a significant delay in the surgery, which pushed the procedure close to closing time. She explained that the delay was due to complications in a previous surgery performed by Dr. Garcia, the surgeon. Dr. Morris also told me, "you wouldn’t want him to leave if your dog was in critical condition," yet that is exactly what happened once they realized they went through with a surgery without having the proper tools to stabilize Cohen.

After the surgery, which was performed by Dr. Garcia, Cohen was in critical condition. Dr. Morris, despite previously stating the tumor was benign based on the biopsy and consultation with the oncologist, was now uncertain whether the tumor was cancerous or benign. At this point, I was told that I would need to personally transport Cohen to an ER vet 30 minutes away (VEG), as Affordable Pet Hospital lacked the necessary equipment and medication to stabilize him, yet they had proceeded with the surgery anyway.  Dr. Garcia also stated that the reason why Cohen was having such difficulty was because he was so small, and the tumor was so large, that his body and internal organs were struggling with adjusting after removing the mass.

As I was preparing to take him to the ER, Dr. Morris increased his dopamine IV from 10 to 12, but struggled with operating the IV machine and had to be guided through its use by the vet techs in the room. I also noticed the tumor on the table behind Cohen, and it appeared to be about half his size, much larger than Dr. Morris had described. Prior to surgery, Dr. Morris also made comments of Cohens weight claiming his was overweight and that he would need to be on a diet and loose weight- including during the time of the ultrasound, biopsy, and other procedures leading up to his surgery. However, now in hindsight, I question how much of his “weight” was due to the tumor he had- which she knew exactly how large it was. Additionally, prior to surgery I expressed my concern of Cohens size and the tumor, and asked if he should be on a medication such as Palladia to decrease the size of the tumor prior to surgery, to which Dr Morris stated it wouldn’t be necessary since it was only taking up a portion of his liver.

After Cohen’s passing, I requested his full veterinary records, which revealed that the tumor extended "from his diaphragm to caudal to the liver," a significantly larger mass than what Dr. Morris had communicated. During our discussions about Cohen’s chances of survival, Dr. Morris had estimated a 50% chance of recovery if we took him to VEG, but tragically, within minutes of leaving Affordable Pet Hospital with Cohen still attached to the dopamine IV on our way to VEG, my sweet boy passed away in my arms.

With this all being said, I advise anyone seeking care for their fur babies to go elsewhere.  Although the vet techs are phenomenal, Dr. Morris does not seem to truly care about anything other than generating money for this facility.
If this were any other profession, she would either have her license revoked, or forced to retire.
